Example:
To apply Sarrus' rule, take the sum of the products of the diagonals from the upper left to the lower right, then subtract the sum of the products of the diagonals from the lower left to the upper right.

Consider matrix B:
 [2, 3, 1]
 B = [4, 5, 6]
 [7, 8, 9]

Using Sarrus' rule, det(B) is calculated as follows:

(2*5*9 + 3*6*7 + 1*4*8) - (1*5*7 + 2*6*8 + 3*4*9) = 90 + 126 + 32 - (35 + 96 + 108) = 248 - 239 = 9

Thus, det(B) = 9, indicating B has an inverse.
